CveFindings.Name: Microsoft.Data.SqlClient and System.Data.SqlClient vulnerable to SQL Data Provider Security Feature Bypass
CveFindings.Description:
[CVE-2024-0056](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-98g6-xh36-x2p7): Microsoft.Data.SqlClient and System.Data.SqlClient vulnerable to SQL Data Provider Security Feature Bypass

Severity: HIGH

Affected dependency:
  - Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 2.1.4 (packages.config:14; affected range: < 2.1.7)

Recommended fix:
  - Upgrade Microsoft.Data.SqlClient to 2.1.7 or later.
CveFindings.Explanation:
[CVE-2024-0056](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-98g6-xh36-x2p7): Microsoft.Data.SqlClient and System.Data.SqlClient vulnerable to SQL Data Provider Security Feature Bypass

Severity: HIGH

Affected dependency:
  - Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 2.1.4 (packages.config:14; affected range: < 2.1.7)

Recommended fix:
  - Upgrade Microsoft.Data.SqlClient to 2.1.7 or later.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.
CweFindings.Explanation: NotificationService instances are constructed for controller requests, and the constructor separately checks MessageQueue.Exists before creating the shared queue. Concurrent first requests can both observe the queue as absent and race to create the same resource; this check-then-create sequence has no synchronization.

CweFindings.Name: Missing Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
CweFindings.Explanation: Each request creates a NotificationService instance that may initialize the same MSMQ queue. The Exists-then-Create operation is not synchronized, so simultaneous requests can race during shared queue initialization.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
CweFindings.Description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.
CweFindings.Explanation: When creating its private notification queue, NotificationService explicitly grants the Everyone principal MessageQueueAccessRights.FullControl. This allows any actor represented by Everyone to read, write, and administer a resource intended for application notifications.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: The Edit action binds TeachingMaterialImagePath from the request and, when an image is uploaded, passes that value directly to Server.MapPath before deleting the resolved file. The path is not validated to remain under the TeachingMaterials directory, allowing path elements such as ../ to resolve outside the intended directory.

CweFindings.Name: Relative Path Traversal
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: The Edit action binds the request-controlled TeachingMaterialImagePath and passes it to Server.MapPath, then File.Exists and File.Delete, without rejecting relative traversal sequences such as ../.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: Course titles are accepted from requests and passed as entityDisplayName when notifications are created. NotificationService.GenerateMessage embeds that value in Message, which is returned by NotificationsController.GetNotifications and inserted into notificationEl.innerHTML without HTML encoding in notifications.js. A title containing markup can execute in the browser of users viewing notifications.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
CweFindings.Description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.
CweFindings.Explanation: The Edit action binds TeachingMaterialImagePath from the request and uses the value as a filesystem resource identifier in Server.MapPath, File.Exists, and File.Delete without verifying it refers to an image beneath the intended upload directory.
